newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil seen lower soon despite rally.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil seen lower soon despite rally.

text.p: The current rally in palm oil prices supported by talk of good Malaysian exports in October may be a last fling by speculators before prices drift off towards the end of the year.
"October's Malaysian figures are going to look good but we expect exports during November and December to be low," said a European trader.
He and others forecast a slow down in demand during the next three months owing to a run of holidays in Europe and Asia.
"Production seems to be holding up better then people expected and demand will slow down between now and the end of February," said a Singapore-based trader.
News that Indonesia is to carry on importing crude palm oil ahead of Christmas and the Moslem fasting month Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr is not expected to affect European prices.
But it has given a further boost to the Malaysian palm oil futures market.

"At the moment the market is futures led and those boys are going to latch on to anything that will keep prices high but this is their last fling before fundamentals take over again," said the Singapore source.
Traders said palm oil is losing its competitiveness against other oils and must come lower to boost business.
"At the moment palm olein is around $535 a tonne fob Malaysia which doesn't look very good against soy, rape and sun oil, all of which are available nearer to $500 a tonne fob," one said.
In the soft oil sector business remains quiet with little buying interest.
"The market is very quiet and needs some fresh news," said a participan.
Concern over genetically-modified U.S. soybeans remains in the background.
But a premium of 4.50 to five guilders for rape oil over soy oil has closed to around 2.50 guilders during the past week.
This was despite news that some major European food producers have said they will not use soy products derived from the modified US soybeans.
